author: Member 2 (Computer Vision & Sonar Processing)
project: AI-Powered Automated Underwater Marine Debris and Anomaly Detection System using Side-Scan Sonar Imagery

execution_order.scientific_justification: Corrects macro acoustic geometric spreading loss (1/R^2) and seawater range attenuation fall-off across the swath. Must precede local operations to prevent biased baselines across near-range vs far-range.
Suppresses high-frequency coherent acoustic speckle in homogeneous sediments while strictly preserving sharp acoustic highlight-to-shadow boundaries. Outperforms Gaussian and Median blurs.
Calibrates pixel intensities to full [0, 255] uint8 dynamic range using 1%-99% percentile clipping, eliminating dynamic range compression caused by single-pixel acoustic spike outliers.
Maximizes local target-to-shadow contrast within 80x80 contextual tiles without blowing out noise floor. Preserves false-color palette integrity by operating strictly on luminance.

rejected_methods.reason_for_rejection: Blindly diffuses high-frequency gradients (EPI 0.322 vs 0.500 for Bilateral), blurring small debris boundaries (e.g. compact targets, mines).
Erodes sharp geometric corners and thin structural boundaries (EPI 0.284), degrading acoustic shadow penumbras.
Spatial kernel dilation washes out acoustic shadows (shadow area reduced to 19.4% vs 20.4% for Lee), lowers PSNR (27.88 dB), and exhibits 4.9x higher latency (231.7 ms).

While Lee 5x5 is effective in isolation (PSNR 30.33 dB), chaining both Lee and Bilateral causes redundant double-smoothing and destroys fine seabed sediment texture. Bilateral filter alone provides higher signal fidelity (PSNR 34.40 dB).

Direct image subtraction strips ambient seafloor contextual textures essential for YOLO feature pyramids. Furthermore, morphological kernels >= 9x9 activate natural sand ripple crests and troughs (12.7% false clutter for 9x9, 26.8% for 15x15), inducing severe false-positive risks for object detectors. Reserved strictly as an auxiliary research feature.
